Ever-expanding federal government stealthily constricting individual freedoms
0 ne of the clear messages of the Republican landslide of 1994 was that the public favors the downsizing of government. What is actually occurring is that government is becoming an ever larger part of our lives - like the stealth bomber, we may not see it at first, but it is there.
Some government policy makers and bureaucrats are working ever harder to ehsure their share of the public purse string. A case In point is the Food and Drug Administration. In early 1995, the FDA was pledging to farm out activities that private agencies could do faster and more effectively and to eliminate regulation that add nothing to public health. Today, however, the FDA is demanding more regulatory powers, requiring a bigger budget and more employees.
David Kessler, the FDA's commissioner, has proven to be an astute pilot of the sicakh bomber, steering so that the public does not see where he's going. The FDA has selected its strategy wisely. The FDA knows that the public is more likely to support increased budgets if the agency claims that it Is supposedly improving health and protecting young people.
The claims of the FDA are smoke and mirrors. The fact is that FDA regulations will not reduce smoking among youth. Research shows that the primary cause of smoking by youngsters is peer pressure -- the desire to be "cool" and to show independence from parents and
